title: Operator state-sanitizer hotfix and customer runbook for on-prem upgrade failures
creator: Marco Li
description:
Summary:
During a staggered rollout of operator v2.3.0 to several on-prem/VPC customers we observed multiple clusters reporting failed post-upgrade reconciliation: CR status fields were cleared, leader-election endpoints flapped, and the node-agent sidecar entered CrashLoopBackOff on clusters with older kubelet versions. Two high-touch enterprise customers opened escalations concurrently; both experienced degraded API surface for their app-engine workloads and one reported >30% increased tail latency on inference endpoints.

Root cause hypothesis and investigation notes:
- The helm pre-upgrade hook (migrator job) in 2.3.0 had a race condition when a customer CRD schema version differed by a patch-level skew; this caused the migrator to partially apply patches and exit with non-zero but non-fatal codes. Helm then continued the upgrade leaving custom resources in a partially-upgraded state.
- Operator reconcile logic in v2.3.0 attempted an aggressive status rewrite that assumed presence of fields created by the migrator; missing fields were overwritten to empty values which caused downstream controllers (leader-election, node-agent) to re-elect and temporarily lose leases.
- Clusters running kubelet <=1.22 showed higher incidence due to slightly different API ordering for init containers, exposing a timing window where the node-agent failed readiness probes while operator was already reconciling.

Work completed so far (technical):
1) Implemented a dedicated "state-sanitizer" subcommand in the operator: a safe, idempotent reconciliation pass that compares live CRs against expected invariants and repairs only missing/invalid status fields without rewriting user-set spec fields. Added strict guards to never drop fields unless explicit migration metadata is present.
2) Introduced an optional post-upgrade atomic helm hook (helm.PostUpgrade -> Job) that runs the sanitizer in a dry-run first, logs a patch preview, then applies changes only if no conflicts are detected. The job includes exponential backoff and write-ahead patch-preview stored as ConfigMap for observability.
3) Fixed the migrator job to validate schema version and fail-fast with clear error codes; added a flag --skip-on-unknown-schema that support may use as a temporary mitigation.
4) Added a preflight check in the helm chart that detects kubelet / api-server version skews against a compatibility matrix and bails with a clear instruction when cluster is outside supported bounds.
5) Created and validated a canary rollout plan using blue/green helm release names and a traffic-splitting ingress hook for customers that opt into staged upgrade.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for sanitizer logic (field-preservation and idempotency) added, coverage >90% for affected modules.
- Integration test harness extended to simulate partial migrator failures and older kubelet versions using KinD nodes with patched kubelets.
- e2e run against a private customer's replica of their cluster (staging) produced zero reconciliation anomalies across 3 consecutive upgrades when sanitizer and post-upgrade job were enabled.

Runbook for Support (short version):
1) Stop further helm upgrades for affected customers and switch them to manual upgrade channel.
2) If CRs show cleared status fields, run operator state-sanitizer in dry-run mode: kubectl -n redwood exec -it job/state-sanitizer -- --dry-run --preview-cm <name>. Review preview ConfigMap.
3) If preview is sane, run sanitizer without --dry-run. Monitor operator logs and leader-election endpoints for 15m.
4) If node-agent CrashLoopBackOff persists, escalate to infra on-call and apply node-agent restart patch (kubectl rollout restart daemonset/node-agent -n redwood).
5) Offer customers a canary re-upgrade using release tag onprem-operator-2.3.1-canary with explicit traffic-split.

Rollback strategy:
- We discourage blind helm rollback due to potential partial migrations. Rollback path: use sanitizer to bring CRs to a consistent known state, then perform a controlled helm rollback to previous operator version. If rollback is attempted without sanitizing, risk of repeated partial state remains.

Communication and approvals:
- Drafted customer-facing incident email template and shareable diff (preview ConfigMap link) for customers to review intended state patches before we apply.
- Product and Legal approved the hotfix communication and opt-in canary program.

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Postmortem and incident writeup scheduled (owners: Aisha) due 2025-11-18.
- Add periodic drift-detection job to console alerts and include an automated ticket in Linear if drift > threshold.
- Expand compatibility tests matrix in CI to include kubelet 1.20-1.25 permutations.
- Document sanitizer API and make it callable from Console with preview UI.

Links and artifacts:
- PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/1427
- Canary deployment playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Onprem+Canary+Upgrade+Playbook
- Customer staging test report: https://drive.redwood.ai/reports/ENG-67890-staging-report.pdf
comments: 2025-11-05 - Marco Li: Created ticket after two customers reported post-upgrade anomalies. Initial triage indicates migrator/helm hook race; assigned to Aisha for remediation and customer coordination.
2025-11-06 - Aisha Raman: Implemented sanitizer prototype and validated idempotency locally. Repro harness shows reproducible partial-migrator failure when CRD version skew is present.

2025-11-07 - SRE reviewer (Daniel Park): Reviewed sanitizer design. Requested additional safety gates: (1) don't patch status fields touched in last 5 minutes, (2) record patch reason in resource annotation. Added to PR.

2025-11-08 - QA (Priya Shah): Ran integration tests on KinD with kubelet 1.22; sanitizer passed, but discovered an edge-case with multi-tenant namespaces where preview ConfigMap exceeded size limits. Aisha added chunking to preview output.

2025-11-09 - Customer Success (Lena Ortiz): Notified affected customers of planned hotfix and offered staging window for canary. One customer accepted immediate canary; second requested scheduled weekend window.
2025-11-10 - Aisha Raman: Opened PR #1427 with sanitizer, migrator fail-fast, and helm preflight. Requesting fast-track review. Patch includes detailed unit tests and migration simulation harness.

2025-11-11 - Engineering Lead (Ravi Menon): Approved fast-track on condition of two independent SRE approvals and QA green in staging. SRE approvals obtained; scheduling canary rollout for 2025-11-12 03:00 UTC.

2025-11-12 - Operations (Aisha Raman): Canary applied to customer 'AcmeBio' staging cluster. Dry-run preview shared; customer approved. Sanitizer applied; operator metrics returned to baseline within 9 minutes. Monitoring shows no leader-election flaps for 30m post-apply. Marking as In Progress -> prepare release.
2025-11-12 - Support Note: Customer 'AcmeBio' confirmed production window request for 2025-11-14. Support ticket linked: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/58432
